children: Next delivered a "pleasant surprise" in its sales figures, but kept its typically cautious profit outlook, Interactive Investor's head of markets Richard Hunter writes in a note. The British retail company's sales for the third quarter rose 8.1% on year. The quarterly performance was strong, with the international business being the standout performer, Hunter says. Still, the group reiterated its forecast of an 8.4% rise in full-year adjusted pretax profit to 1.255 billion pounds. "Next remains optimistic but not cavalier and its guidance is typically conservative," Hunter says, adding that this could weigh on the stock given "high market expectations." Shares are up 0.7%. (andrea.figueras@wsj.com)
